title: The Hobbit Eternal: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: "Yes, I am coming," said Frodo. "The Ring-bearers should go together."
"The love of the Elves for their land and their works is deeper than the deeps of the Sea. Yet they will cast all away rather than submit to Sauron—for they *know* him now."
Hood and cloak were gone; they were in shining armor, and red light leapt from their eyes. In the gloom the great Dwarf gleamed like gold in a dying fire.
"Here is the heart of Elvendom on earth, and here my heart dwells ever." —Aragorn
"If we stayed and did nothing, doom would find us anyway. That is why we are marching now." —Treebeard
The Sword of Elendil was forged anew by Elvish smiths.
"Always after a defeat and a respite, the Shadow takes another shape and grows again." —Gandalf
It was the Guarded City, with walls so strong and old they seemed to have been carved out of the bones of the earth.
Many desired to see the house of Elrond, and breathe the air of that deep valley where the Fair Folk dwelt in peace.
While the Tree grew and blossomed, Queen Arwen sang a song of Valinor.
"'Live and learn!' as my gaffer used to say. Though he was thinking of gardening, not of roosting like a bird, nor of trying to walk like a spider." —Sam
All of them, the ponies as well, grew refreshed and strong in a few days at the Last Homely House.
To the air he had returned, bringing ruin, turning hope to despair, and victory to death.
All was well, until one day they met a thunderstorm—more than a thunderstorm, a thunder-battle.
Bilbo's return was quite unexpected, met with confusion and worry but also wonder and awe.
Elvish singing was not a thing to miss, in June under the stars.
At Midsummer in the year of the Fall of Sauron, Aragorn took the hand of Arwen Undómiel, and they were wedded in the city of the Kings.
"The dark fire will not avail you, flame of Udûn."
"The ruffians are on top—gathering, robbing, bullying, and running or ruining things as they like, in his name." —Frodo
"Great Kings take what is their right."
He goes on living, never looking a day older.
There in that pleasant corner of the world, the Hobbits plied their well-ordered business of living.
With strength of arms, Bard demonstrated the might once possessed by the old lords of Dale.
His hatred for Dwarves smoldered for years after they killed his father Azog. When they killed the Great Goblin, the embers became a blaze.
In haste Dáin had come to his kinsman's aid, and in fury he now defended him.
"Slash them! Beat them! Bite them! Gnash them!"
Even before Bard sent for aid, the Elvenking knew of Smaug's death and had already made plans to march.
Before all went Aragorn with the Flame of the West—Andúril, like a new fire kindled, Narsil reforged as deadly as of old. And upon his brow was the Star of Elendil.
The sword glinted in the westering sun.
"Gondor is in great need. Lord Denethor asks for all your strength and all your speed, lest Gondor fall at last."
"Where now the horse and the rider? Where is the horn that was blowing? Where is the helm and the hauberk, and the bright hair flowing?" —Lament for the Rohirrim
"What roads would any dare to tread if the Dúnedain were all gone into the grave?" —Aragorn
"Cold be hand and heart and bone, and cold be sleep under stone: never more to wake on stony bed, never, till the Sun fails and the Moon is dead."
He passed over Udûn and Gorgoroth and saw all the land in ruin and tumult beneath him, and before him Mount Doom blazing.
In a twinkling the table was laid. There was hot soup, cold meats, a blackberry tart, new loaves, slabs of butter, and half a ripe cheese: good plain food, as good as the Shire could show.
The Dead awaken; for the hour is come for the oathbreakers.
"The Orcs were greater in number than we counted on. Great Orcs, who also bore the White Hand of Isengard." —Éomer
"There is a great fleet drawing near to the mouths of Anduin, manned by the Corsairs of Umbar in the South. They have long ceased to fear the might of Gondor." —Beregond
"And in the night from Otherworld beyond the Sea there strong and free a storm arose . . ." —*Song of Eärendil*
It was an old tradition that beyond the Shire stood the Grey Havens, from which at times elven-ships set sail, never to return.
"If you will try to run away you must be tied; but we don't wish to hurt you." —Sam
After their reunion, the Hobbits spent many days in Ithilien. The stream that flowed from the falls of Henneth Annûn could be heard in the night as it rushed down through its rocky gate.
And so the companies came and were hailed and cheered and passed through the Gate.
"Look on us now with friendly eyes! Behold the trees of the Naith of Lórien and be glad!" —Haldir
"But there are some of us still who go abroad for the gathering of news and the watching of our enemies." —Haldir
"The Corsairs are upon us! Back to the walls! Back to the City before all are overwhelmed!"
"Fool of a Took! This is a serious journey, not a Hobbit walking-party. Throw yourself in next time, and then you will be no further nuisance. Now be quiet!"
Frodo's voice was blown away by the willow-wind and drowned in a clamor of leaves.
"I tried to take the Ring from Frodo. I am sorry. I have paid." —Boromir
"You should not look in when the candles are lit." —Gollum

It seemed to the tenders of the sick that on the Halfling and on the Lady of Rohan this malady lay heavily. Soon they began to fall down into the darkness, and as the sun turned west, a grey shadow crept over their faces.
"Curse the Isengarders! Uglúk u bagronk sha pushdug Saruman-glob búbhosh skai!"
Frodo was hardly less terrified than his companions; he was quaking as if he was bitter cold, but his terror was swallowed up in a sudden temptation to put on the Ring.
As Frodo put on the Ring, Sauron was suddenly aware of the magnitude of his own folly. His wrath blazed in consuming flame, but his fear rose like black smoke.
"A great cave-troll, I think. There is no hope of escape that way." —Gandalf
"An Orc shot Balin from behind a stone. We slew the Orc, but many more came." —*Book of Mazarbul*
The barricade was scattered as if by a thunderbolt.
"But the Orcs have brought a devilry from Orthanc." —Aragorn
"Let us hope that fire now lies between us and pursuit. Come! There is no time to lose." —Gandalf
"I have looked on Moria, and it is very great, but it has become dark and dreadful." —Gimli
"'For a couple o' pins,' says Troll, and grins, 'I'll eat thee too and gnaw thy shins.'" —Sam
"I daresay there's more truth in some of them stories than you reckon." —Sam
Trolls were abroad, no longer dull-witted, but cunning and armed with dreadful weapons.
"No living man am I!"
His eyes were keen as lances in starlight, and yet profound, the wells of deep memory.
"I sang of leaves, of leaves of gold, and leaves of gold there grew: Of wind I sang, a wind there came and in the branches blew."

"The Three Rings of the Elves were not made as weapons of war or conquest—that is not their power. Those who made them did not desire strength or domination or hoarded wealth, but understanding, making, and healing, to preserve all things unstained." —Elrond
"Do not think that only by singing amid the trees, nor even by the slender arrows of Elven-bows, is this land of Lothlórien maintained and defended against its Enemy." —Galadriel
"I shall lead you well, and the paths are smooth and straight."
"That was the custom of the Elves of Lórien, to dwell in the trees. Therefore they were called Galadhrim, the Tree-people." —Legolas
All that is gold does not glitter, Not all those who wander are lost; The old that is strong does not wither, Deep roots are not reached by the frost.
"I'm leaving; for somewhere where I can finish my book, perhaps. I have thought of a nice ending for it: 'And he lived happily ever after to the end of his days.'" —Bilbo
